A year.

Okay.

Right.

So we do both sides, but it's obviously quite informative of both sides of the deals that we, that we see.
And because we do work in the US as well, we obviously see the larger deals and multiples as well because they, they tend to pay a little bit more over there.
So, yeah, so that's us.
I've been doing this about seven years.

Well, I'll share.

It was a relationship.

Don't do as much as that.

So we used to turn educational, for example universities, we'd take them from a regional provider to a national provider.

So as MDS moves, they tend to take us with them.
I'll give you a couple of examples.
We have lanes for drains.
I'll just give that as an example because they're out there in the market and they've grown, they've just sold the business for half a billion.
We had a relationship with them for 10 years.
We were fundamental in growing those revenues for them prior to the sale.
Yeah.
And there were 80 million when we started working.
80 million when we started with them.
Yeah.
So half a billion.
The turnover was half a billion.
Sorry, the turnover was half a billion.
Yeah, sorry.
So that relationship only came to an end because they stopped all supply relationships while they were building more profit in the business.
However, we were fundamental to the growth of that company.
We managed all of their depots.
There was about 30 and we would take underperforming depots and put them back into profit and we would manage the profitable depots and double the turnover.
So we managed the whole, if you like, sales process on their behalf and we managed the business development managers and supported them on a national footprint.
Other companies.
Last year, wasn't it?
That finished last year.
Yes, that only finished last year due to them being up for sale.
Other companies, small business.

We love those types of businesses.
So one customer very focused on the domestic market, been in that sector for 20 years, wanting to go into the commercial sector and grow.
They came on board with us and in the first eight months of being with us we generated over a million pounds worth of revenue for them.
That was in 2024.

Logistics company worked with this guy.

Logistics business.

And the outcome of it was S3PL says we have a team of 12.
How have you achieved this in three years to sell the business?
And the answer was because we had a contribution, a significant contribution from Heather Carter and Simon Carter's team.
So we still, at this moment in time still work for that company.
And.
Then we'll have other businesses where, you know, they are looking well.
Manufacturing company, Japanese company, very, very large organization.
They have a manufacturing company in printers.
They came to us and said, we're too dependent on our resellers.
We don't really know what they're doing.
We've got an international footprint.
We've never had a sales process embedded into our organization.
Can you help us?
And that's how we started the relationship with them.
And from then now we have been working with them for.
Would it be 12 months time coming up to something like that?
18, actually about 18.
So we've created and refined a sales process for them.
We manage their resellers and they are restructuring their sales division on the back of our contribution for the future.
And we're working in France and Germany as well.
And we're working in France and Germany.
We do do international too.
So we're all remote workers.
We have an international footprint.
We have an international team.
Some of our team have been with us 15 to 23 years, just at three or four folk or two or three folk, I can't remember now.
And we just at that stage of our business, we, many years ago we went through this process with a company.
We weren't very happy with what we experienced, if I'm honest with you.
So it's took a lot, especially for me to even come on a call with you because it, we found it incredibly distracting.
Yeah.
And it's actually really cost us our business.
And we had to start again at.
The time, didn't it?
We, we, we ended up focusing on the sale process for probably six months.
And at the end of it, the company that was potentially acquiring us took our MD and he went to IT directly for them.
And you know, all our customers that we were working with dropped off because they hadn't had our personal attention for that six months.
And you know, it was just, it.
Was a, it was, it was a nightmare.
Yeah, it was an absolute nightmare.
There are lessons, there are lessons there.
But yeah, unfortunately there's always lessons there actually.
And do you know something?
Nothing is a bad experience.
It makes you the person you are today.
So there's, there's no sim.
You know, I am sorry for ourselves there.
It was just the experience at the time.

But where we are now, we are in a tech business and we have a purpose within that and we put incredible personal wealth in it as well as have some investment into the company and that has an amazing future ahead of it.

So Simon and I are both in the 60s, so we're at that stage of life where we're making certain decisions and I suppose really we've got to this decision that, you know, do we flip our sales and marketing growth agency into our tech business to drive sales?

Because, you know, if I sell this business, I wouldn't really want to be the one running the business.
I want somebody to go, we've got fantastic MD here, fantastic sales team and actually you've got great credentials and we'd like to lift and shift it and put it into our business.
So we're kind of in that mode of thinking of where do we go and what do we do.
So we're not desperate to sell, but we're looking for ideas.
Is it something.

So, you know, we're there or thereabouts or could be if we stopped taking the money out and putting it into our technology business.
To your criteria, but probably are smaller than, you know, the typical companies that you're working with.
Yes, we work with companies of all different sizes.
On the sell side.
Yeah, I mean particularly on agencies because we operate as a, as a brokerage.
So we're essentially, yeah, just put.

Okay, so.

The.

We might for the year.
Do you, do you know what you.
Last year?
Yeah.

Okay.
And the profit from that is roughly what, quarter of a million?
Yeah, that's what I'm saying about.
Yeah.
To 25.
Most of which we're putting into the technology business at the moment.
Take and take out as revenue further.

You know it's a, it's a popular add on for lots of companies.

So, so, so they, they are looking for Legion more often than not.
So that's a good space to be in.
Right.
And I think because you've been working in B2B as well and obviously the, the, you know, the standard of your clients very high with Lloyds and things like that.
So.
Yeah, yeah.
I mean the Japanese companies are conglomerate.
Six billion pound conglomerate.
You know, it's a prop customer and we, you know, we've got more services.
I'm sure we could sell a lot more into it, you know.

But it's just what you want to get out of it because obviously it affects the price.

So what was that, Andy, Just out of curiosity?
Well, you know, what were they?
What size of business were they that you sold?

They were really good growth projections for the year but they knew that they could smash them.
So it was a good deal for everybody basically.
Okay.

I would say just off the, you know, just on the face of it, you're probably looking at somewhere between a 4, 4 and a 5 multiple.

That's all.

Yeah.

Yeah.

Yeah.

Yeah, but, but given the complexities of that then you know, potentially it might knock the valuation a little bit.

Etc.
So but yeah, roughly speaking I would say, you know, you're somewhere between a four and a five times multiple.
So you know, back the fag packet valuation is you're somewhere around 1.2 million, something like that, maybe a bit more.
So obviously the way that would be structured is half that in cash up front and then I mean if we were to do a 12 month earn out, the rest of it on, on the earn out.
Okay, something like that.
Does that sound about Right.
Or is that too low for what you're looking for?
Are you looking at me, Simon?
Yeah.
Yeah, I suppose I haven't got any expectations at this moment in time.
I'm still very driven, Andy, and ambitious so you know, I haven't really thought about what that needs or should look like at this moment in time.
The 12 month appeals to me because I know that I would be required to be in the business as part of that transition period.
You know so that, that's for consideration.
Your sales aren't you.
So if they need a sales base then then yes, you definitely would be.
But you don't know that that would.
No, you don't know.
You don't know.
No, no, not at all.
No, you don't.
Yeah.
I mean it.
Until we find the buyer, it's difficult to know what their motivations are as well.
I mean different, different things going on.
So they could just be looking for your clients, could just be looking for your staff or your systems or whatever.
Yeah, we've got an operational guy so you know, he's a CEO and yeah, he, he's, he's, he's his corporate background.
Into his corporate background.
He ran a thousand seat center for Vodafone years ago and 500 for a company operated out of Bosnia recently for Shell.
So you know he's got a good.
Blue chip, he's got a pedigree anti behind him.
Really.
Yeah.
So.
Okay.
Well I mean it's that kind of ballpark I would say.
I don't like to over egg valuation so I would say it's probably quite conservative.
We hear a lot about the states getting far, far bigger marketing contracts.
So I think that's one of the reasons the multiples are higher out there.
Is that the way you would say that we should exit just literally sell and then we can move on with our lives?
Or would you say it's better trying to do kind of a reverse.
I think, I think people do over complicate them.
I think given where you are.
Yeah, I wouldn't bother with that sort of stuff.

I mean it's, you're just going to add a couple of years onto whatever you're looking at anyway so you know you're motivated to exit this business for something else that's got a higher return for you so you know to add on more complications and again, you know some of those things could go wrong so you could acquire another business.
It could go badly.
It could damage the, you know, it could damage the valuation that you have already.
So.
Yeah, and it might just, you know, might, might cause further problems or issues in the business that take longer to resolve before you get to a point where you can.
Yeah.
You know, even to have the brain space to go through the exit.
Struggling a little bit with this PR agency, haven't we?
Have.
We have really.
Yeah.
There's some great bits but you know, it is a challenge even bringing that.
Well again, you know, it's small and it won't really move the dial that much.
So you know, if you were to double the size of the business then of course, you know, instead of being a four to five times multiple, I would say that could go up to a six or a seven.
Particularly if you had a founder in the other business that was willing to stay on for three years.
Yeah, you're a better valuation but, but it's not that.
It's just the 500k, you know, it's not really going to drive the need for the acquirer than what you've got at the moment.
You've got a lead gen business and that's what companies like to acquire.
PR businesses actually are a lot more 10 a penny.
You know, they're harder to keep stable because they're often founder based.
You know, all the relationships, founder and the names with the founder.
Yeah.
So, you know, it probably is not really going to bring anything to the table and just add some complication.
So I would say great to hear.
Yeah.
Nothing else come out of this call that's worth it for that alone actually.
So, yeah, thank you for that.
So I've got a couple of minutes and then I've got to jump onto my last call of the night.
What I'll just say is we have a couple of ways to do it.
We do have like a full process that we can run but it's, it's more expensive and there's a level of risk to you.
But I would say probably the sensible way to work with us, we have like a prep for market package, it's 5, $5,000, 4,000 roughly.
And for that we will do a proper valuation.
My team will dig into your financials and we will have a proper sort of considered valuation where we go to market with a proper idea.
We've been through your accounts and we will suggest some ways of tweaking that value as well by putting things in, taking things out.

And we also prepare what's called an IM or a, a SIM some people call it, which is a confidential information memorandum, which is just kind of a pitch deck that, you know, you go to Market with pitch deck for bankers.
And we put all of that together for you.

Plus we do your listing and then we market to not only our mailing list, but also we will look for buyers that are in this space, you know, or not just within our network, but actually build a list, bespoke list of potential buyers, you know, give them what your clients might be, the fact you're based in Spain, etc.
We're going to look a bit more, more into it rather than if it was just a listing on agencies where it just goes out to our mailing list.
Okay, so that's five, $5,000 to do that.
Like I said, we prep the whole thing.
We'll handhold the entire way through it.
We're looking for a buyer probably about three or four months into the process to sort of raise a hand.
And then once we have that buyer, we're able to leverage that against all the other interests that we've got.
And the idea really is two or three offers on the table and get the business sold within six months.
That's what we're, we're looking to do in terms of a process.
So I can put that into an email for you and ask.
Yeah, let's do that.
Can I ask a question, if you don't mind?
What is, what is your success rate of selling companies like ours of yours.
Is closer to 100% than some of the more complicated companies?
Yeah, we've, we've had a really good run of Legion companies.
We just sold a company in Los Angeles and it was actually, it wasn't even profitable, but we had, I think it was 45 signed NDAs in, in 24 hours, which is a record for us.
But it was a combination of factors.
But certainly the fact it was lead gen.
Right.
Was a big part of it.

Yeah, I, I did wonder because I have seen a lot of agencies for sale and I did wonder with all the AI piece that's coming in now and I get it all and all the rest of it and it's all wonderful, some of it, but that humanness is very, it's still attractive to people.
Yeah.
You still need to think it's different.
Yeah.
Even with all the AI and automation there, there still needs to be somebody that can sell it, you know, somebody that can translate that into an offer for, for clients and.
Yeah.
To run the thing.
So, yeah, I don't think it will remove the founders, but it just takes away the number of staff that you need to execute, doesn't it?
Yeah.
I'll send an email and I'll fire it off to you.
I think you bought our course as well, did you, Simon?
I did, yeah.
I've done some of it, yeah.
Not all of it.
Okay, I think I still owe you a conversation on that one as well.
So if you need to have half an hour with me and go through and acquisition strategy, I'm happy to do that too.
Okay, fantastic.
Thanks, Andy.
Lovely meeting.
Forward to speaking soon.
Thank you very much.
Thank you.
All right, enjoy the rest of your evening.
You too.
Get better soon.
One more.

summary.overview: During the Business Development and Consultation meeting between Heather Carter and Andy Day, key insights were shared regarding their respective business backgrounds and current opportunities. Andy, representing Capital A Group, an M&A advisory focused on US clients, introduced their service offerings, including the unique Agencies Co platform for agency transactions. Simon detailed his growth specialist company's extensive experience, including a successful partnership with Lloyds TSB and notable achievements such as significantly boosting Lanes for Drains' revenue. The discussion then shifted to valuation and exit strategies, with Andy providing an estimated business valuation of £1.2 million, and recommending a straightforward sale approach over more complex strategies. Action items were established, including Andy following up with details about his 'prep for market' package, while Simon was tasked with reviewing an acquisition strategy course and planning a potential follow-up call.
summary.short_summary: During the Business Development and Consultation meeting, Heather Carter and Andy Day exchanged insights about their businesses and explored potential opportunities. Andy, from Capital A Group, specialized in M&A advisory for US clients, showcased their unique Agencies Co platform tailored for agency transactions. Simon, representing a growth specialist company, highlighted their successful collaboration with Lloyds TSB and their impressive track record, including a significant revenue boost for Lanes for Drains. The conversation then transitioned to valuation and exit strategies, where Andy estimated a business valuation of £1.2 million and advocated for a straightforward sale approach instead of complex strategies. They identified action items, such as Andy providing details about his 'prep for market' package and Simon reviewing an acquisition strategy course, while also considering a follow-up call.
